For a symmetric actual wing with both old factors nontrivial its precise alternative is strict 2i>|A|+2, or |B|=5, right rank2/order10, |A| even and i=|A|/2+1. Its faithful restriction and character filter are actual accepted premises, not an assumed quotient IP. The new manuscript reproduces that interface exactly.

In Lemma1 the parent is explicitly a string C-marking in v2. The even symmetric wing inherits actual fracture and IP; its rank m/2+1 meets the boundary theorem. For m=4, rank3 disconnected string implies an isolated central mark, impossible in S4; larger degrees use the normal-factor obstruction. The adjacent last split transfers with a trivial factor, while interior wing splits are nonadjacent to the parent cut.

If the first wing split is at0, its complementary actual wing has degree m-1 and rank m/2, so the already proved individual nonsymmetric-wing bound forces full Sym(m-1). Its first anchor comes from its own split; its last anchor is the original attachment, distinct from the removed singleton because different end marks move them. It inherits omissions and has connected diagram, including the explicit S3/rank2 case. The two-anchor inequality is 2(i-1)=m>m-1.

All resulting indices in Lemma1 are checked: j=1 transfers adjacently into the full wing with a trivial near factor, then nonadjacently to the parent because i>=3. For j>=2 first use nonadjacent transfer into the wing; j=i-1 is then adjacent at the old parent cut and pays its trivial factor, while other j lie in1..i-2. No recursive theorem is used here.

In the opposite-end lemma, actual symmetric supports C union D and D union B, together with full IP, give T=<rho3,...,rho_(i-1)>=Sym(D). Thus its transitivity is proved. Its rank t=m/2-2 and degree d=m-5 obey 2t=d+1. The m=6 case is impossible because it would put one nonidentity mark on a singleton. For m=8 the middle is exactly the explicitly covered S3 rank2; larger odd d have connected symmetric diagrams.

The cuts remain perfect inside each symmetric wing because the actual middle T is transitive and each crossing mark fixes the opposite five-point region. This validates both successive omission transfers. The inner crossing endpoints are fixed by all but the corresponding nearest middle mark; transitivity forces those nearest marks to move them, supplying the two anchors.

At j=3 or j=i-1 the adjacent middle-wing transfer satisfies 2t=d+1>d-1 and produces a trivial factor; the second transfer to the whole parent is nonadjacent since t>=2. For4<=j<=i-2 both transfers are nonadjacent. The resulting two sides are C plus a nonempty part of D and B plus its other nonempty part, hence both exceed five. All claimed index intervals and fixed support additions hold in the m=8 boundary.

The strong induction is on actual symmetric degree with actual fracture retained. For degrees5,6 the acquired complete extremal classification leaves the ordinary simplex; the degree6 outer action is excluded by its transitive omissions. No degree below5 can satisfy the strict rank inequality and the acquired rank<=degree-1 bound. Every inductive wing is a proper support, inherits IP/fracture, and has the exact strict threshold required. Its usable internal split lies in1..wingrank-2, so nonadjacent inheritance preserves the trivial factor.

After moving the critical even-wing split, the new regions are C,D,B with D nonempty and old |B|=5. If the new symmetric wing is on C, the opposite support has size |D|+5>5, ruling out the sole augmentation exception. A second exceptional case can therefore only have symmetric wing D union B, with |C|=5 and left rank2, forcing k=2. Since the old right rank is2, i=r-3, and both symmetric wings have the same even degree m and rank m/2+1. These are exactly the opposite-end lemma hypotheses.

If that lemma yields sides both larger than five and neither factor trivial, either symmetric wing chosen by the acquired theorem must satisfy strict descent: neither opposite side has the exceptional size five. There is no induction at equal degree. Split moves and opposite-end treatment are finite in-case steps; every recursive call strictly decreases the symmetric degree. The final initial-fracture invocation is confined to n>=7. A usable split here only has the declared support property, not the unpaid leaf-kernel or counting-bijection conditions.
